recommended_sampling: At 2 fps every spine shows up in at least 2 frames in 4 of the 5 videos, and median visibility is about 3-4 frames per book. It is not enough for 20260912_213052, where the pan is fast (about 700-800 px/s): The Fountains of Paradise is in a single blurred 2 fps frame, and several thin spines get only 1-2 blurred frames. The Fodor teknős book (212925), Márquez (212903) and Tunézia/Mozart letters (213028) are in only 2 frames each. Motion blur limits legibility more than coverage does. Blur bursts reach 1000 px/s in 213118 at t≈2.7-3.9 s, and a run of five thin spines there stayed unreadable in every native frame. Recommendation: decode at 6-10 fps (or native 30 fps), then keep the sharpest frame by horizontal-gradient or Laplacian variance within each 0.25-0.33 s window (about 3-4 fps effective). Read thin or small-print spines from full-resolution rotated crops of the sharpest nearby native frame, not the fixed 0.5 s grid. Do not go below 2 fps: at 1 fps thin spines are missed or seen once, blurred. Note that ffmpeg input seeking (-ss before -i) was not frame-accurate on these files. Use select=between(t,...) or decode sequentially when locating exact frames.
hard_cases: 212903 Doyle: the thin black pocket-series spine is motion-blurred. Readers split between 'Tanulmány vörösben' and 'Tanulmány vérvörösben'. Word length in rotated crops supports 'VÉRVÖRÖSBEN'.
212903 Ferrante vol. 4: 'elveszett' vs 'elvesztett' is a one-letter difference that a fuzzy matcher may hide. The spine clearly says 'Az elvesztett gyerek története'.
212903 Factfulness: a reader wrote publisher Scolar (the Hungarian publisher of the translation), but the spine logo is Sceptre (English edition). This is publisher metadata only.
212925 Salamon Gábor / Zalotay Melinda: the typewriter font makes S and Z look alike, and one reader produced 'Balamon/Balotay'.

212925 'A jól nevelt görög teknős': a very thin, blurred spine in 2 frames. Both readers got the author wrong ('Fábián Attila' or just 'Attila'); the real author is Fodor Attila, which only fits the blurred 5-letter shape. A pipeline will likely need external lookup here.

212925 vs 213028 Matyszak 'Antik Róma napi öt denáriusból': the same edition appears in two videos, but on different shelves with different neighbours. Treated as two physical copies, not a duplicate; the duplicate detector should not merge these by title alone.
212925 two identical 'Anya, taníts engem!' copies side by side should count as 2 books.

213028 Mozart spines: a narrow, shorter 'Mozart, az Isten kegyeltje' (Michel Parouty) stands against the wider Sadie 'MOZART | Grove monográfiák'. Perspective makes the red line look like a subtitle, and one reader merged the two spines.

213028 script-lettered pink spine: both readers agreed on 'Mozart Bäsle-levelei', a plausible-sounding but apparently non-existent title. Enhanced crops fit 'Mozart bécsi levelei' (Gondolat Aurora, 1960). Reader agreement can still be wrong.
213028 'Olyan kicsi krumplik vagyunk…': no author on the spine and possibly a mistaken Peanuts association. It is the Salamon–Zalotay bilingual quote book.
213028 'Az én Fellinim': the author name was at the frame edge in the 2 fps frames, so one reader left it null. It is readable in a native frame (Bernardino Zapponi).

213052 The Swerve vs The Swarm: a black spine with swash-script title, heavily blurred, where readers produced two different real books. Letter count, two-line author block and Vintage logo favour Stephen Greenblatt's The Swerve, but confidence is only moderate.
